candidates.name: Cathédrale St-André
candidates.content: Grand church built from 1170 in Gothic style. It was trashed during the Revolution but restored from 1803. You can climb the detached bell-tower "Pey-Berland".

candidates.name: Musée D'Aquitaine
candidates.content: Brilliant museum with exhibits from the Old Stone Age through Roman times to the early modern period.

candidates.name: Musée des Beaux-Arts
candidates.content: An enlightening walk through the history of western art. Start in the south wing which runs from the Renaissance via the Flemish masters to end of 18th century. The north wing continues through the major 19th and early 20th-centur

candidates.name: Basilique Saint-Michel
candidates.content: Flamboyant Gothic church built from the 14th to 16th century, with detached bell-tower.

candidates.name: Église Sainte-Croix
candidates.content: This was built in the 11th / 12th century as a Benedictine abbey church, and was renovated in the 19th.

candidates.name: Musée d'Art Contemporain
candidates.content: Remarkable building, the Entrepôt Lainé is a huge 19th warehouse for food imports. Most of the space is given over to changing exhibitions and installations (and prices are reduced whenever there isn't one). Display of the permane

candidates.name: Jardin Botanique du Jardin Publique
candidates.content: Started as a garden of medicinal herbs in 1629, the present garden dates from 1858 and covers 0.5 ha. This is the original now specified as "du Jardin Publique". In 2003 an offshoot garden de la Bastide was opened across the river

candidates.name: Musée National des Douanes
candidates.content: Surprisingly informative museum of border control and customs, and their smuggler opponents, down the centuries. Signage only in French, non-francophones should get the audioguide.

candidates.name: Musée Mer Marine
candidates.hours: Tue-Sun 13:00-19:00 (opens at 10:30 during French school holidays)
candidates.content: Extensive museum of shipping and the sea.

candidates.name: Muséum de Bordeaux - sciences et nature
candidates.content: Extensive natural history museum on three floors.

candidates.name: Musée du Vin et du Négoce
candidates.content: History, old equipment and new technology from 2000 years of wine production in the region. The entry fee includes a taste of two wines. (grape juice for children)

candidates.name: MADD-Musée des Arts décoratifs et du Design de Bordeaux
Base sous-marine
candidates.content: Wartime submarine pens, now used for art installations.

candidates.name: Jeux Barjo
candidates.content: Bar specialising in board games ancient and modern: you pay for either one long or three short games. Staff assist if you want to try a game you're not familiar with. They also stage tournaments.

candidates.name: Dick Turpin's
candidates.content: English style pub with good drink and music, relaxed friendly vibe.

candidates.name: El Chuchumbe
candidates.content: Latin bar serving inexpensive mojitos, and towards midnight it becomes a salsa dance floor.

candidates.name: The Frog and Rosbif
candidates.content: English pub with micro-brewery in a 16th century women's prison, a popular gathering spot for live TV sports.

candidates.name: Le Café Brun
candidates.content: Atmospheric old bar with a huge selection of whiskies and Belgian beers.

candidates.name: Space Factory
candidates.content: Craft beer bar

candidates.name: Brique House Bordeaux
candidates.content: Originally from Lille this popular Taproom-restaurant is now in Bordeaux.

candidates.name: MAMACAM
candidates.content: Food made with local products. Always vegetarian options.

candidates.name: Chat Noir Cha Vert
candidates.content: Pleasant place for light bites and views of the basilica.

candidates.name: Beirut Kitchen
candidates.content: Good mezze and other Levantine fare.

candidates.name: Chez Ta Mère
candidates.content: As the name suggests, they serve rustic home-style cuisine.

candidates.name: Remparts Café
candidates.content: Charming bistro a few steps from the cathedral.

candidates.name: L'Autre Petit Bois
candidates.content: Quirky sandwich cafe, generous portions, gets crowded.

candidates.name: L'entrecôte
candidates.content: A city institution, no reservations and you'll probably have a long wait in line. What you get is a walnut salad, two pieces of entrecôte steak and unlimited fries, plus dessert and wine. Most customers reckon it's worth the wait.

candidates.name: Café Populaire
candidates.content: Relaxed restaurant, then it morphs into a dad-dancing arena.

candidates.name: Le Café du Port
candidates.content: Great views of Pont de Pierre and the left riverbank. Good dining to match, they often host events.

candidates.name: Couleur Cafe
candidates.content: Mostly positive reviews for this bistro by the cathedral.

candidates.name: Chez Faty
candidates.content: Delicious lunchtime couscous and tajine.

candidates.name: Restaurant Soléna
candidates.content: Outstanding French / Oriental cuisine. The chef is Victor Ostronzec.

december.text: thumb | 300px | The ice rink is at Mériadeck
Ice hockey: Boxers de Bordeaux play in Ligue Magnus, the French top professional league. They play at Meriadeck ice-rink, which also hosts public skating and ice-karting.
